title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
text: heuristic distance Barratt’s unsupervised mixture-model distance. pair isolates \((, k)\) locus \(j\), per-locus delta \(\delta_{ik}^{(j)}\) computed; overall distance sum per-locus deltas.

title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
text: pair isolates share comparable locus (missing) contribute sum. Barratt’s two-pass mean procedure fills entries: isolate missing locus, find complete isolates whose allele sets match every non-missing locus. Impute missing-locus delta mean matched isolates’ deltas. match exists, impute using global mean locus. second pass catches rows remain partially empty first pass, re-imputing first-pass results. final distance pair \((, k)\) : \[ D_{ik}^{(H)} = \sum_{j=1}^{L} \delta_{ik}^{(j)} \]

title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
text: Plucinski’s naive-Bayes distance evaluates, pair \((, k)\), three log-likelihoods per locus corresponding three relatedness hypotheses.

title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
text: Let \(\mathbf{v}_{ij}\) allele values (set, actual observed alleles, multiplicities) carried isolate \(\) locus \(j\), let \(p_{ja}\) empirical frequency allele \(\) . Hypothesis 0 — unrelated: isolates draw alleles independently locus allele frequencies: \[ \ell_0 = \sum_{\\mathbf{v}_{ij}} \log p_{ja} +           \sum_{\\mathbf{v}_{kj}} \log p_{ja} \] Hypothesis 1 — share one allele: pair shares exactly one allele; shared allele likely one. every pair positions \((u, v)\) \(v_{iju} = v_{kjv}\), compute: \[ \ell_{1,uv} = \ell_0 - \log p_{j,v_{iju}} \] take \(\ell_1 = \max_{uv} \ell_{1,uv}\). shared allele exists, \(\ell_1 = \log(\epsilon \cdot \min(p_{\text{obs}}))\), \(\epsilon\) estimated allele-capture failure rate (default 0.3072, estimated Joel Barratt May 2019) \(\min(p_{\text{obs}})\) smallest frequency among alleles carried pair. Hypothesis 2 — share alleles (diploid loci ): isolates share pair alleles (multiset equality). every pair 2-subsets \((\mathbf{}, \mathbf{b})\) \(\mathbf{v}_{ij}\) \(\mathbf{v}_{kj}\) equal multisets: \[ \ell_{2,\mathbf{}\mathbf{b}} =   \bigl(\ell_0 - \log p_{j,a_1} - \log p_{j,a_2}\bigr) +   \sum_{\\mathbf{v}_{kj}} \log p_{ja} \] \(\ell_2 = \max \ell_{2,\mathbf{}\mathbf{b}}\). multiset equality exists: \[ \ell_2 = \log\bigl[(\epsilon \cdot \min(p_{\text{obs}}))^{2 - n_{\text{shared}}}\bigr] \] \(n_{\text{shared}}\) number distinct allele values shared two subsets.

title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
text: per-locus log-likelihoods summed across loci: \[ s_0 = \sum_{j} \ell_0^{(j)}, \quad s_1 = \sum_{j} \ell_1^{(j)}, \quad s_2 = \sum_{j} \ell_2^{(j)} \] normalised posterior three hypotheses: \[ \Pr(h \mid \text{data}) = \frac{e^{s_h}}{e^{s_0} + e^{s_1} + e^{s_2}}, \quad h \\{0, 1, 2\} \] distance posterior expected number shared-allele hypotheses: \[ D_{ik}^{(B)} = 0 \cdot \Pr(0) + 1 \cdot \Pr(1) + 2 \cdot \Pr(2) \[0, 2] \] Values near 0 indicate pair appears unrelated; values near 2 suggest complete allelic sharing.

title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
text: heuristic Bayesian distances operate different scales different sensitivities. ensemble combines via fractional rank averaging, copula-style summary invariant monotone transformations either distance. \(n \times n\) distance matrix \(D\), let \(U\) set \(\binom{n}{2}\) unordered upper-triangular entries. Assign fractional ranks: \[ r(D)_{ik} = \frac{\text{rank } D_{ik} \text{ among } U}                  {|U| + 1} \] \(r(D)_{ik} \(0, 1)\). ensemble entry : \[ D_{ik}^{(E)} = \frac{r\bigl(D^{(H)}\bigr)_{ik} +                     r\bigl(D^{(B)}\bigr)_{ik}}{2} \] Values near 0 indicate methods agree high similarity; values near 1 indicate strong divergence.

title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works

what: What is MLST and why distance matrices?
title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: Multilocus Sequence Typing (MLST) characterises microbial isolates alleles present set housekeeping loci. Given collection samples (isolates), potentially multiple alleles per locus (due heterozygosity, mixed infections, polyploidy), central question : genetically similar two samples? fasteukaryotyping implements three-method ensemble described Barratt et al. (2019) (doi:10.1017/S0031182019000581) computing pairwise genetic distances MLST haplotype data sheets (HDS).
code: library(fasteukaryotyping)

title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: Barratt’s unsupervised heuristic mixture-model distance computes, locus, delta value depends number shared alleles, allele-set sizes, per-locus entropy term \(H_{\nu}\), frequency-informed penalty \(P\). per-locus deltas summed across loci produce pairwise distance. Missing loci imputed two-pass mean procedure matches original Barratt script.
code: set.seed(42) n <- 10 geno <- list(   matrix(sample(c(1L, 2L, 3L, NA), n * 2, replace = TRUE), nrow = n, ncol = 2),   matrix(sample(c(1L, 2L, NA), n * 2, replace = TRUE), nrow = n, ncol = 2) ) d_h <- euk_heuristic_distance(geno, ploidy = c(2L, 2L)) dim(d_h) ## [1] 10 10

title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: Plucinski’s naive Bayes genetic distance evaluates, pair locus, three log-likelihoods: ll0: samples unrelated – every allele drawn independently locus allele frequencies. ll1: samples share exactly one allele – shared allele likely one; remaining alleles drawn independently. ll2 (diploid loci ): samples share alleles – evaluated 2-subsets; missing allele draws get probability \(\epsilon \cdot \min(p_1, p_2)\). per-locus values summed, normalised posterior three hypotheses, distance posterior expectation \([0, 2]\).
code: d_b <- euk_bayesian_distance(geno, ploidy = c(2L, 2L)) dim(d_b) ## [1] 10 10

title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: ensemble converts matrix fractional ranks unordered pairs takes mean two ranks. copula-style average invariant monotone transformations either distance, producing consensus value \([0, 1]\).
code: d_e <- euk_ensemble_distance(geno, ploidy = c(2L, 2L)) dim(d_e) ## [1] 10 10

title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: core input geno list \(L\) integer matrices (one per locus), \(n\) rows (samples) maxMOI columns. Missing alleles coded NA (0). ploidy vector specifies whether locus haploid (1) diploid (2). MLST data often stored Haplotype Data Sheet (HDS): CSV Seq_ID column one column per haplotype per locus, presence marked "X". Use euk_import_hds() convert format internal geno list:
code: hds <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "example_hds.csv",                              package = "fasteukaryotyping"),                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE) out <- euk_import_hds(hds, locinames = "Hap", ploidy = 2L) attr(out, "geno") ## [[1]] ##       1_Hap_Hap 2_Hap_Hap ##  [1,]         1         1 ##  [2,]         2         2 ##  [3,]         1         1 ##  [4,]         2         2 ##  [5,]         1         1 ##  [6,]         1         1 ##  [7,]         2         2 ##  [8,]         2         2 ##  [9,]         1         1 ## [10,]         2         2 ## [11,]         1         1 ## [12,]         2         2

title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: C++ implementation uses RcppParallel multi-threaded pairwise computation. dataset \(n\) samples \(L\) loci, heuristic distance processes \(\binom{n}{2}\) pairs parallel per locus, Bayesian distance parallelises full \(n \times n\) matrix. Compare R reference C++ implementations built-example:
code: eg <- example_eukaryotyping system.time({   d_r <- euk_heuristic_distance(eg$geno, eg$ploidy, use_r = TRUE) }) ##    user  system elapsed  ##   0.020   0.000   0.021 system.time({   d_cpp <- euk_heuristic_distance(eg$geno, eg$ploidy, use_r = FALSE) }) ##    user  system elapsed  ##       0       0       0

title: fastEukaryotyping 0.1.0
text: Initial package skeleton. Pure-R reference implementation euk_heuristic_distance_r(). C++17/RcppParallel implementation euk_heuristic_distance_impl(). Added impute_data flag euk_heuristic_distance() reference implementation. Pure-R reference euk_bayesian_distance_r() porting Plucinski’s euk_bayesian_fulldataset_V2.r, including epsilon fallbacks multiset/unique-overlap pair semantics original. C++17/RcppParallel implementation euk_bayesian_distance_impl(). euk_bayesian_distance() matches original script output 68-sample fixture within 1e-10 (R C++ backends). euk_ensemble_distance(): rank-mapped mean heuristic Bayesian matrices, per original ensemble workflow.
